subject: Residency addendum proposal & proposed failover window
messages:
From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@medsys.health>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@medsys.health>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency addendum + temporary failover window (MedSys)

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. MedSys is ready to move forward but our privacy team has two asks before legal will sign the DPA: a written addendum committing to EU-only residency for all production workloads, and a narrowly-scoped failover window policy for cross-region processing during unavoidable operational incidents.

Specifically:
- Can Redwood commit to storing all persistent customer data for MedSys within EU regions only (we can provide specific AWS region list)?
- As an exception, we may accept transient processing or failover to non-EU regions for incident response, but we need the window limited (please propose a maximum duration and notification SLA) and full telemetry/audit evidence for any occurrence.
- Please provide an updated subprocessor roster and confirmation that any non-EU subprocessors will not have access to EU-pinned production data except under the documented failover process.

I attached a redline of the current DPA with comments (MedSys_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf). Can you review and propose text we can use for a short addendum? Also CC'ing our technical lead Tom if you want to coordinate telemetry/ops details.

Best,
Samantha Cole
Head of Privacy
MedSys Health

Subject: Re: Data residency addendum + temporary failover window (MedSys)

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear asks and for the redline. We're very aligned on minimizing cross-border exposure and can propose an addendum that captures EU-pinning plus a tightly-scoped operational failover process. Looping in Laura (legal) and Priyom (solutions) to draft recommended language and the telemetry/ops checklist. Marissa will coordinate next steps on the contracting timeline.

Quick answers up front:
- EU residency: Redwood can commit to storing persistent customer data in EU regions for MedSys production environments. We will list the canonical AWS regions we use and provide a subsection that allows MedSys to pin a subset of regions you specify.
- Failover window: we suggest a default maximum of 72 hours for emergency cross-region processing with mandatory customer notification within 2 hours of the event being initiated and a post-incident audit report within 5 business days. If you'd prefer a shorter window (48 hours), happy to propose language.
- Subprocessors: we'll share the latest roster and include a clause that restricts non-EU subprocessors from accessing EU-pinned persistent data except during an invoked failover under the addendum. Priyom will attach a topology diagram and list of technical controls for telemetry.

Attachments: redwood-region-topology.png (ops topology), dpa-addendum-draft.docx (initial draft from legal).

I'll wait for Laura/Priyom to follow up with concrete draft text.

—Karthik

Karthik / team —

Thanks — couple of technical clarifications from our side before Laura's legal language:
1) When you say "pin a subset of regions", can you confirm the mechanics? Will traffic and storage be geo-bound at the service level (single region deployment) or will you use multi-AZ within a single region? We need guarantees about cross-region backups and replication.
2) Failover telemetry: the post-incident audit must include request-level traces (timestamps, model id, route, originating region, list of compute nodes involved) and an itemized list of data egress locations for every request processed outside EU.
3) For the roster: please indicate whether any analytics/observability subprocessors are US-based and whether they can receive hashed telemetry that contains EU customer identifiers.

If you can answer those, we can expedite legal sign-off. Attached is our annotated list of the EU regions we want to pin.

Subject: Re: Data residency addendum + temporary failover window (MedSys)

Samantha / Tom —

Appreciate the detailed notes. Based on internal review and Priyom's topology, we've prepared a short DPA addendum draft (attached) and the operational commitments below for inclusion in the DPA annex. Please treat this as our proposal — happy to revise wording.

Proposed commitments (high level):
1) EU Residency Commitment: Redwood will retain persistent customer data for MedSys production workloads in the following EU regions only: eu-west-1 (Ireland), eu-central-1 (Frankfurt), eu-west-3 (Paris). Customer may request an explicit subset pin during onboarding; Redwood will not transfer or replicate persistent customer data to non-EU regions except as described in section 2.

2) Emergency Failover (scope and limitations):
   - Trigger: Failover may be invoked only during documented, non-routine operational incidents (major regional outage, active-severity incident impacting availability) and requires Redwood incident commander approval plus immediate notification to MedSys policy contacts.
   - Duration: Default maximum combined cross-region processing duration per incident is 48 hours. Extensions beyond 48 hours require written customer approval.
   - Notification SLA: Customer will be notified via email and PagerDuty within 2 hours of invocation.
   - Evidence / Audit: For any cross-region processing event, Redwood will provide an audit package within 5 business days containing per-request trace logs (request id, timestamp, model id, originating region, egress region, compute instance id), a list of subprocessors that accessed data during the event and sanitized examples of logs. Logs will be provided in hashed/obfuscated form where required by Redwood's security policy; raw logs can be made available under a controlled audit review if contractually approved.

3) Subprocessor Access Controls:
   - Non-EU subprocessors are contractually prohibited from accessing persistent EU-pinned production data except when a documented failover is invoked.
   - Analytics/observability providers will only receive pseudonymized telemetry by default; raw identifiers will not be shared without explicit customer consent or as required during a documented incident for debug/audit purposes.

4) Acceptance and Implementation:
   - We propose adding this as DPA Addendum A, with an operational runbook (Annex 1) that Priyom will supply detailing telemetry fields, retention for audit packages, and redacted examples.

Next steps: if you confirm the 48-hour window is acceptable we will circulate a redline of the DPA with Addendum A and the runbook. If you require 24 or 72 hours instead, let us know and we'll mark that as an open term. Once terms are agreed, Marissa will coordinate contract timing and DocuSign.

Regards,

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
